An engine is attached to a wagon through a shock absorber of length $1.5 {\text{m}}$. The system with a total mass of $40000 {\text{kg}}$ is moving with a speed of $72 {\text{kmh}}^{-1}$, when the brakes are applied to bring it to rest. In the process of the system beingbrought to rest, the spring of the shock absorber gets compressed by $1.0 {\text{m}}$. If $90 \%$ of energy of the wagon is lost due to friction, the spring constant is ............. × $10^{5} {\text{N}} / {\text{m}}$.
explanation: Given, the length of the shock absorber, I = 1.5 m The total mass of the system, M = 40000 kg The speed of the wagon, v = 72 km/h When brakes are applied, the final velocity, $\text{v}_\text{f}$ = 0 The compressed spring of the shock absorber, x = 1mApplying the work-energy theorem, Work done by the system = Change in kinetic energy W = Δ KE $\text{W}_{{\text{friction} }}+\text{W}_{{\text{spring} }}=\frac{1}{2} \text{m} \text{v}_{\text{f}}^{2}+\frac{1}{2} \text{m} \text{v}_{\text{i}}^{2}$ $-\frac{90}{100}(\frac{1}{2} \text{m} \text{v}^{2})+\text{W}_{{\text{spring} }}=0-\frac{1}{2} \text{m} \text{v}_{\text{i}}^{2}$ (∵ 90% energy lost due to friction) $\text{W}_{{\text{spring} }}=-\frac{10}{100} ×\frac{1}{2} \text{m} \text{v}^{2}$ $-\frac{1}{2} \text{k} \text{x}^{2}=\frac{1}{20} \text{m} \text{v}^{2}$ $\text{k}={\text{m} \text{v}^{2}}/{10 ×x^{2}}$ Substituting the values in the above equation, we get $\text{k}={40000 ×(72 ×\frac{5}{18})^{2}}/{10(1)^{2}}$ = 16 × $10^5$ N / m Comparing the spring constant, k = x × $10^5$ The value of the x = 16.

question_text: A body of mass m dropped from a height h reaches the ground with a speed of $0.8 \\sqrt{\text{gh}}$. The value of workdone by the air-friction is
explanation: Given, the mass of the body = m The height from which the body dropped = h The speed of the body when reached the ground, $\text{v}_{\text{f}}=0.8 \\sqrt{\text{gh}}$ Initial velocity of the body, v = 0 m / s Using the work-energy theorem, Work done by gravity + Work done by air-friction = Final kinetic energy - Initial kinetic energy $\text{W}_{{\text{mg} }}+\text{W}_{{\text{air}- \text{friction} }}=\frac{1}{2} \text{m} \text{v}_{\text{f}}^{2}-\frac{1}{2} \text{m} \text{v}_{\text{i}}^{2}$ Here, work done by gravity = mgh ⇒ $\text{m} \text{g} \text{h}+\text{W}_{{\text{air}-\text{friction} }}=\frac{1}{2} \text{m}(0.8 \\sqrt{\text{g} \text{h}})^{2}-\frac{1}{2} \text{m}(0)^{2}$ ⇒ $\text{W}_{{\text{air} - \text{fricion} }}=\frac{0.64 \text{m} \text{g} \text{h}}{2}-\text{m} \text{g} \text{h}$ = 0.32 mgh - mgh = -0.68 mgh The value of the work done by the air friction is -0.68 mgh.

question_text: A block moving horizontally on a smooth surface with a speed of $40 {\text{m}} / {\text{s}}$ splits into two parts with masses in the ratio of $1: 2$. If the smaller part moves at $60 {\text{m}}/ {\text{s}}$ in the same direction, then the fractional change in kinetic energy is
explanation: Let a block of mass M splits into two masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ in ratio 1: 2. Then, mass of smaller part, $m_{1}=\frac{\text{M}}{1+2}=\frac{\text{M}}{3}$ Mass of bigger part, $m_{2}=2 \text{M} / 3$ Given, speed of mass M, v = 40 m/s Speed of mass $m_{1}, v_{1}=60 {m} / {s}$ Let speed of mass $m_{2}, v_{2}=v$ Using conservation of linear momentum, ${p}_{i}={p}_{\text{f}}$ $\text{M} {v}=m_{1} {v}_{1}+m_{2} {v}_{2}$ $\text{M} ×40=\frac{\text{M}}{3} ×60+\frac{2 \text{M}}{3} ×v$ ⇒ = 30 m/s ∴ The fractional change in kinetic energy, $\frac{\Δ\text{K}}{\text{K}}={\text{K}_{\text{f}}-\text{K}_{i}}/{\text{K}_{i}}={\text{K}_{\text{f}}}/{\text{K}_{i}}-1$ $={\frac{1}{2} m_{1} v_{1}^{2}+\frac{1}{2} m_{2} v_{2}^{2}}/{\frac{1}{2} \text{M} v^{2}}-1$ $={\frac{1}{2}[\frac{\text{M}}{3} ×(60)^{2}+\frac{2 \text{M}}{3}×(30)^{2}]}/{\frac{1}{2} \text{M} ×(40)^{2}}-1=\frac{9}{8}-1=\frac{1}{8}$

question_text: A block moving horizontally on a smooth surface with a speed of $40 {\text{ms}}^{-1}$ splits into two equal parts. If one of the parts moves at $60 {\text{ms}}^{-1}$ in the same direction, then the fractional change in the kinetic energy will be x: 4, where x is
explanation: Given, initial speed of block, $u=40 {\text{ms}}^{-1}$ Let total mass of block = m ∴ Broken masses, $m_{1}=m_{2}=\frac{m}{2}$ Final speed of $m_{1}, v_{1}=60 {\text{ms}}^{-1}$ As we know that, kinetic energy, ${\text{KE}}=1 / 2 {mv}^{2}$ ∴ Initial kinetic energy ${\text{KE}}_{i}=\frac{1}{2} m u^{2}$ $=\frac{1}{2} m(40)^{2}=800 m$ ...(i) By using law of conservation of momentum, $m u=m_{1} v_{1}+m_{2} v_{2}$ $∴ v_{2}=\frac{m ×40-m / 2 ×60}{m / 2}$ $=\frac{10 m}{m / 2}=20 m s^{-1}$ So, final kinetic energy ${\text{KE}}_{\text{f}}=\frac{1}{2} m_{1} v_{1}^{2}+\frac{1}{2} m_{2} v_{2}^{2}$ $=\frac{1}{2} \frac{m}{2}(v_{1}^{2}+v_{2}^{2})=\frac{m}{4}(60^{2}+20^{2})$ $=m / 4(3600+400)$ $=1000 m$ ...(ii) ∴ Divide Eq (ii) by Eq. (i), we get ${{\text{KE}}_{\text{f}}}/{{\text{KE}}_{i}}={1000 {\text{m}}}/{800}=\frac{5}{4} {\text{m}}$ So, x = 5

question_text: Two persons A and B perform same amount of work in moving a body through a certain distance d with application of forces acting at angle 45° and 60° with the direction of displacement respectively. The ratio of force applied by person A to the force appliedby person B is ${1}/{\\sqrt{x}}$. The value of x is ........ .
explanation: Given, work done by both person is same, $\text{W}_{\text{A}}=\text{W}_{\text{B}}$ Direction of first force with displacement, $\θ_1$ = 45° Direction of first force with displacement, $\θ_2$ = 60° Ratio of force applied by person A to force applied by person B is $\text{F}_{\text{A}}: \text{F}_{\text{B}}=1: \\sqrt{x}$. Work done by both person is same, $\text{W}_{\text{A}}=\text{W}_{\text{B}}=$ $⇒ \text{F}_{\text{A}} \text{d} \cos \θ_{1}=\text{F}_{\text{B}} \text{d} \cos \θ_{2}$ (∵ distance is same for both = d) ${\text{F}_{\text{A}}}/{\text{F}_{\text{B}}}={\cos \θ_{1}}/{\cos \θ_{2}}=\frac{\cos 60°}{\cos 45°}$ $⇒ {\text{F}_{\text{A}}}/{\text{F}_{\text{B}}}={\frac{1}{2}}/{{1}/{\\sqrt{2}}}={1}/{\\sqrt{2}}$ $⇒ {\text{F}_{\text{A}}}/{\text{F}_{\text{B}}}={1}/{\\sqrt{x}}={1}/{\\sqrt{2}}$ $⇒ x=2$ Thus, the value of x is 2.

explanation: We know that, Power $=$ force $×$ velocity $[ ∵$ Given, power $=$ constant $]$ $∴$ Force $×$ velocity $=$ constant $⇒ \;\; m a × v=$ constant $⇒ \;\; a × v=$ constant $⇒ \;\; (v \;\frac{d v}{d x})(\;\frac{d x}{d t})=C ⇒ ∫ v d v=∫ C d t$ $⇒ \;\; \;{v^{2}}/{2}=C t ⇒ v=\sqrt{2 C t}$ $⇒ \;\; \;\frac{d x}{d t}=\sqrt{2 C t}$ $[ ∵ v=\;\frac{d x}{d t}]$ $⇒ \;\; ∫ d x=∫ \sqrt{2 C t d t} ⇒ x=\sqrt{2 C}(\;{t^{3{/ } 2}}/{3 {/ }2})$ $⇒ \;\; x ∝ t^{3{/ }2}$

question_text: - A boy is rolling a $0.5 {kg}$ ball on the frictionless floor with the speed of $20 {ms}^{-1}$. The ball gets deflected by an obstacle on the way. After deflection it moves with $5 \%$ of its initial kinetic energy. What is the speed of the ball now ?
explanation: Given, mass of rolling ball, $m=0.5 {kg}$ Speed of ball, $u=20 {ms}^{-1}$ Before deflection, Initial kinetic energy, ${KE}_{1}=\;\frac{1}{2} m u^{2}$ $=\;\frac{1}{2} × 0.5 ×(20)^{2}$ $=\;\frac{1}{2} × 0.5 × 400=\;\frac{1}{2} × \;\frac{1}{2} × 400=100 {J}$ It is given in the question that after deflection the ball moves with $5 \%$ of its initial kinetic energy ${KE}_{f}=5 \%$ of ${KE}_{ {i}} ⇒ {KE}_{f}=\;\frac{5}{100} × 100=5 {J}$ If the final speed of the ball is $v {ms}^{-1}$, then ${KE}_{f}=\;\frac{1}{2} m v^{2}$ $⇒ \;\; 5=\;\frac{1}{2} × 0.5 × v^{2} ⇒ 10=0.5 × v^{2}$ $⇒ \;\; v^{2}=\;\frac{10}{0.5}=\;\frac{100}{5} ⇒ v^{2}=20$ $⇒ \;\; v=\sqrt{20}=4.47 {ms}^{-1}$ $⇒ \;\; v=4.47 {ms}^{-1}$

Of the four choices given after the Statements, choose the one that best describes the two Statements.If two springs $S_1$ and $S_2$ of force constants $k_1$ and $k_2$, respectively, are stretched by the same force, it is found that more work is done on spring $S_1$ than on spring $S_2$.STATEMENT 1: If stretched by the same amount work done on $S_1$, Work done on $S_1$ is more than $S_2$STATEMENT 2: $k_1< k_2$
options: A. Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true
B. Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
C. Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is true, Statement 2 is the correct explanation for Statement 1
D. Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is true, Statement 2 is not the correct explanation for Statement 1
explanation: We know force $(F)=k x$ $\;W=\;\frac{1}{2} k x^2$ $\;W=\;\frac{(k x)^2}{2 k}$ $\; ∴ W=\;\frac{F^2}{2 k}[\;\text{ as }\; F=k x]$When force is same then,$W ∝ \;\frac{1}{k}$Given that, $W_1>W_2$ $∴ k_1< k_2$ Statement-2 is true.For the same extension, ${\text{x}}_1= {\text{x}}_2= {\text{x}}$Work done on spring ${\text{S}}_1$ is ${\text{W}}_1=\;\frac{1}{2} k_1 x_1^2=\;\frac{1}{2} k_1 x^2$Work done on spring ${\text{S}}_2$ is ${\text{W}}_2=\;\frac{1}{2} k_2 x_2^2=\;\frac{1}{2} k_2 x^2$ $∴ \;\frac{W_1}{W_2}=\;\frac{k_1}{k_2}$As $k_1< k_2$ then $W_1< W_2$So, Statement-1 is false.

question_text: A $2 {\text{kg}}$ block slides on a horizontal floor with a speed of $4 {\text{m}} {/} {\ s}$. It strikes a uncompressed spring, and compress it till the block is motionless. The kinetic friction force is $15 N$ and spring constant is $10,000 {\text{N}} {/} {\text{m}}$. The spring compresses by
explanation: Let the block compress the spring by $x$ before coming to rest. Initial kinetic energy of the block $=$ (potential energy of compressed spring) $+$ work done due to friction. $\;\frac{1}{2} × 2 ×(4)^2=\;\frac{1}{2} × 10000 × x^2+15 × x$ $10,000 x^2+30 x-32=0$ $⇒ 5000 x^2+15 x-16=0$ $∴ x=\;{-15 ± {\sqrt{(15)^2-4 ×(5000)(-16)}}}/{2 × 5000}$ $=0.055 m=5.5 {\text{cm}}$

question_text: A ball of mass $0.2 {\text{kg}}$ is thrown vertically upwards by applying a force by hand. If the hand moves $0.2 {\text{m}}$ while applying the force and the ball goes upto $2 {\text{m}}$ height further, find the magnitude of the force. (consider $g=10 {\text{m}} / {\ s}^2$ ).
explanation: According to energy conservation law,Work done by the hand and due to gravity = total change in the kinetic energyInitially the the ball is at rest and finally at top its velocity become zero so total change in kinetic energy $∆ K=0$ $W_{\;\text{hand }\;}+W_{\;\text{gravity }\;}=∆ K$[Here distance covered would be $0.2$ meter for force by hand as force is applied while ball is in contact with hand.And gravity will still work while ball is in contact with hand so total distance due to gravity would be $2+0.2=2.2$ meter. $]$ $⇒ F(0.2)-(0.2)(10)(2.2)=0 ⇒ F=22 N$ $∴$ Option (D) is correct.

Potential energy (P.E.) $;=\;\frac{1}{4}-\;\frac{1}{2}=-\;\frac{1}{4} J$ $\;K ⋅ E ⋅(\max .)+P ⋅ E ⋅(\min .)=2$ 𝜕(Given) $\; ∴ K ⋅ E ⋅(\max .)=2+\;\frac{1}{4}=\;\frac{9}{4}$ $\; ∴ \;\frac{1}{2} m v_{\max }^2=\;\frac{9}{4}$ $\;⇒ \;\frac{1}{2} × 1 × v^2{ }_{\max .}=\;\frac{9}{4}$ $\;⇒ v_{\max }=\;{3}/{{\sqrt{2}}} {\text{m}} {/} {\ s}$

explanation: Let $K$ be the initial kinetic energy and $F$ be the resistive force. (i) and (ii) we get,$\;\frac{x}{3}=\;\frac{1}{3}$ or $x=1 {\text{cm}}$

question_text: A particle moves in a straight line with retardation proportional to its displacement. Its loss of kinetic energy for any displacement $x$ is proportional to
explanation: Given that, retardation $∝$ displacement$⇒ a=-k x$But we know $a=v \;\frac{d v}{d x}$ $\; ∴ \;\frac{v d v}{d x}=-k x$ $\;⇒ ∫↙{v_1}↖{v_2} v d v=-k ∫↙{0}↖{x} x \text{dx}$ $\; (v_2^2-v_1^2) =-k \;\frac{x^2}{2}$ $\;⇒ \;\frac{1}{2} m (v_2^2-v_1^2) =\;\frac{1}{2} m k (\;\frac{-x^2}{2})$ $∴$ Loss in kinetic energy is proportional to $x^2$.$∴ ∆ K ∝ x^2$

question_text: A body is moved along a straight line by a machine delivering a constant power. The distance moved by the body in time ${ }^{'} t$ ' is proportional to
explanation: We know that $F × v=$ Power According to the question, power is constant. $∴ F × v=c \;\;$ where $c=$ constant $∴ m \;\frac{d v}{d t} × v=c \;\; ( ∴ F=m a=\;\frac{m d v}{d t})$ $∴ m ∫↙{0}↖{v} v d v=c ∫↙{0}↖{t} \text{dt} \;\; ∴ \;\frac{1}{2} m v^2=c t$ $∴ v=\sqrt{\;\frac{2 c}{m}} × t^{1 / 2}$ $\;\frac{d x}{d t}=\sqrt{\;\frac{2 c}{m}} × t^{1 / 2} \;\;$ where $v=\;\frac{d x}{d t}$ $∴ ∫↙{0}↖{x} \text{dx}=\sqrt{\;\frac{2 c}{m}} × ∫↙{0}↖{t} t^{1 / 2} \text{dt}$ $x=\sqrt{\;\frac{2 c}{m}} × \;{2 t^{5 / 2}}/{3} ⇒ x ∝ t^{3 / 2}$

If a body looses half of its velocity on penetrating $3 {\text{cm}}$ in a wooden block, then how much will it penetrate more before coming to rest?
explanation: We know the work energy theorem, $W=∆ K=F S$ For first penetration, by applying work energy theorem we get, $\;\frac{1}{2} m v^2-\;\frac{1}{2} m(\;\frac{v}{2})^2=F × 3 . . .(i)$ For second penetration, by applying work energy theorem we get, $\;\frac{1}{2} m(\;\frac{v}{2})^2-0=F × S$....(ii) On dividing $(i i)$ by $(i)$ $\;\frac{1 / 4}{3 / 4}=S / 3$ $∴ S=1 {\text{cm}}$

question_text: A ball whose kinetic energy E, is projected at an angle of $45^{∘}$ to the horizontal. The kinetic energy of the ball at the highest point of its height will be
explanation: Assume the ball of mass $m$ is projected with a speed $u$. Then the kinetic energy(E) at the point of projection $=\;\frac{1}{2} m u^2$ At highest point of flight only horizontal component of velocity $u \cos θ$ present as at highest point vertical component of velocity is $=0$. Note : The horizontal component of velocity does not change in entire projectile motion. At highest point the velocity is $=u \cos θ=u \cos 45^{∘}=\;{u}/{\sqrt{2}}$ $∴$ The kinetic energy at the height point $=\;\frac{1}{2} m(\;{u}/{\sqrt{2}})^2$ $=\;\frac{1}{2} m u^2 × \;\frac{1}{2}=\;\frac{E}{2}$

question_text: A spring of force constant $800 {\text{N}} {/} {\text{m}}$ has an extension of $5 {\text{cm}}$. The work done in extending it from 5 ${\text{cm}}$ to $15 {\text{cm}}$ is
explanation: When we extend the spring by $d x$ then the work done $d W=k x d x$ Applying integration both sides we get, $∴ W=k ∫↙{0.05}↖{0.15} x d x$ $=\;\frac{800}{2}[(0.15)^2-(0.05)^2]$ $=8 J$
